Activate sustained formalization of Route 02. Start with the finite accounting theorem and continue toward deriving the energy identity from geometric remainder estimates. Read and execute the launch prompt in:

/smooth-poincare-4d/formalization/investigations/02_neck_energy_accounting/continuation-notes/CONTINUATION.md

I’ll read the Route 02 launch prompt, check the existing Lean declarations and manuscript hypotheses, then formalize the accounting theorem and follow its geometric dependencies as far as the evidence supports.

The manuscript and dependency pins match the launch baseline. The opening finite theorem now elaborates. I’m connecting it to a measure-theoretic proof that charges every uncovered point and takes the source limit before exhausting the components.

Lean now proves the energy identity from finite component measures, convergence on fixed truncations, and estimates for the strips and uncovered mass. It also proves that, without those estimates, the iterated complementary mass is exactly the energy defect. I’m checking how the manuscript’s chiral densities and annular bounds supply those inputs.

The accounting proof now accepts full Weyl energy estimates on physical strips. Lean verified the local factor of \(1/4\) converting those estimates to positive chiral energy, and the volume change under a smooth comparison map. The counterexample checks also confirm that an uncontrolled gap to the next prescribed scale can retain positive mass.

The single-cut work now supplies a definition of the positive Weyl block from the metric’s Levi–Civita curvature. I’m using it to strengthen the fixed-truncation theorem so that its convergence hypothesis refers to curvature components of actual metrics.

The fixed-domain proof now uses the actual curvature tensor and Riemannian volume. I also found a theorem in the pinned geometry library that takes metric two-jet convergence to full Riemann curvature convergence. I’m checking the composition in moving oriented frames, including the volume Jacobian.

Lean has verified two inputs that previously had to be supplied separately: Gram–Schmidt gives convergent oriented orthonormal frames, and the metric Gram determinant gives the correct volume Jacobian. The fixed-domain integral still needs measurable densities and an integrable bound on the weighted full curvature.

Route 02 now has a Lean proof of the finite accounting theorem and a derivation of the energy identity from estimates on the geometric remainder.

Let \(e\) be the limiting source energy, \(e_0\) the base energy, and \(e_j\) the bubble energies. Under convergence on fixed truncations, Lean proves that the entire energy defect is the mass left outside their images:
\[
e-e_0-\sum_j e_j
=\lim_{L\to\infty}\limsup_{i\to\infty}\mu_i(R_{Li}).
\]
The order matters: the source index \(i\) tends to infinity at fixed truncation \(L\). If the total strip estimate and the mass left uncovered by the strips both vanish in this order, the energy identity follows. With the component gap and strict residual hypotheses, every bubble has zero energy and the base carries \(e\).

The formalization also reaches the **actual metric energy on a fixed compact domain**. Intrinsic \(C^2\) metric convergence yields convergent oriented orthonormal frames, curvature coefficients, and volume Jacobians. Measurability and a common integrable bound on the weighted full curvature square then give convergence of the chiral energy integrals.

The remaining global step is to obtain comparisons and estimates covering the full remainder of an almost Bach-flat sequence. In particular, control along one ALE end can leave a gap before the next prescribed scale.

The default build passed. The audit checked **115 declarations, including 85 theorems**, using only standard Lean axioms. The blueprint and repository link checks passed. Chat capture remained unavailable.
